question: Can a domain-grounded multi-agent system autonomously formulate, execute, verify, and iteratively refine mechanistic-interpretability research, producing reliable causal findings and interventions across language, multimodal safety, and biological sequence models?

key_findings.claim: Mechanist packages mechanistic research into an artifact-mediated four-stage loop: hypothesis generation, experiment execution, verification, and revision.
key_findings.evidence: A central orchestrator parses objectives, resources, and schedules, then invokes isolated stage agents. Structured files carry claims, plans, code, results, and integrity reports across stages; the verifier audits leakage, labels, metrics, artifact provenance, and robustness across methods, data, or models, while an iteration agent routes defects back to hypothesis or experiment design until success or a revision budget is exhausted.

key_findings.claim: Domain-specific retrieval and method scaffolding are the system's main claimed advantage over general coding or AI-scientist agents.
key_findings.evidence: Mechanist combines SciAtlas's 43-million-paper, 26-discipline graph with an approximately 13,000-document interpretability graph organized by study object, application, and method, then retrieves via query decomposition, BM25, dense and HyDE matching, bounded graph expansion, reciprocal-rank fusion, and reranking. A library of 32 executable methods across 11 families supplies method assumptions, failure modes, and adjustment rules.

key_findings.claim: In a 16-paper blinded reconstruction benchmark, Mechanist is judged more reliable than Claude Code and AI Scientist, especially on execution and methodology.
key_findings.evidence: Systems receive a target claim but cannot access its paper or repository. Human judges score Mechanist at 87.2% for data use, 83.3% for design, 92.2% for execution, and 86.5% for analysis, about 9-13 points above Claude Code and 31-38 above AI Scientist. Three human experts, Claude Opus 5, and GPT-5.6-sol all rank Mechanist first overall; examples attribute gains to using the specified mechanistic method and calibrating steering strength on held-out data.

key_findings.claim: The system reports cross-modal subliminal transfer: a teacher's unsafe or fruit preference can affect a student even after overt target content is filtered from the student's training set.
key_findings.evidence: A lab-safety student tuned only on responses classified safe gives unsafe answers on 48.6% of 133 multimodal questions, versus 20.3% untuned and 18.3% for a regular-teacher control. A text-to-image student trained on 164 banana-filtered outputs from a banana-preferring teacher generates bananas for 25.6% of 160 preference prompts, versus 2.5% untuned and 2.1% for the regular-teacher control; each reported arm uses three training runs.

key_findings.claim: Mechanist localizes partially separable attention-head mechanisms for reporting another person's belief and preserving factual knowledge under a conflicting belief context.
key_findings.evidence: In Pythia-1B, ablating attributed-belief head L4.H1 lowers attributed-belief accuracy from 0.86 to 0.34 while personal-belief accuracy stays 0.71 and Pile perplexity changes 7.96 to 8.05. Ablating three personal-belief correction heads lowers personal-belief accuracy from 0.78 to 0.21, raises attributed-belief accuracy to 1.00, and changes perplexity to 8.23. Random head and parameter masks have little effect, and analogous heads are reported in Pythia-2.8B and OLMo.

key_findings.claim: A lightweight frame router can turn the belief-head localization into targeted inference-time steering with fewer broken answers than prompt hints.
key_findings.evidence: A frozen-model MLP probe classifies queries as world knowledge, personal belief, or attributed belief from two adjacent residual-stream layers and scales the relevant heads, with a world-knowledge guardrail. Net accuracy gains are +15.3, +8.8, and +3.5 points for Pythia-410M, 1B, and 2.8B, versus +1.6, +3.1, and +0.1 for oracle-style hints; break rates are 1.4%, 1.4%, and 1.1% on initially correct items.

key_findings.claim: Mechanism-guided steering of an existing Evo2 sparse-autoencoder feature increases predicted alpha-helical content in generated proteins, but only up to a validity boundary.
key_findings.evidence: Across 900 generated DNA sequences, targeted steering raises mean predicted alpha-helical content from 43.8% unsteered to 56.6%, while random-feature steering gives 43.2%. At pLDDT at least 0.4 the values are 58.7%, 45.4%, and 45.2%; at pLDDT at least 0.5 they are 56.9%, 45.6%, and 45.8%. Increasing the steering coefficient to 8 adds 12.8 points while largely preserving valid open reading frames, but stronger steering degrades ORF validity.

method.core_idea: Specialize an AI-scientist loop for mechanistic interpretability by grounding hypothesis search in structured literature, constraining experiments with executable analysis skills, and making causal validation and artifact provenance explicit stages.
method.mechanism: The hypothesis agent decomposes a user objective into behavior, mechanism, or application claims and retrieves interdisciplinary evidence. The experiment agent expands atomic claims into datasets, splits, models, causal methods, controls, metrics, success criteria, and compute budgets, then performs a small sanity run before full execution. The verifier checks data and label provenance, metric validity, completion artifacts, and robustness to alternate models, methods, or datasets. A separate iteration agent combines these findings with an independent model review and sends scientific-scope problems upstream or implementation problems back to execution. Stage-scoped files, completion markers, append-only review memory, and global conclusion memory make the process resumable and discourage duplicate hypotheses.
assumptions: Retrieved literature and automatically extracted knowledge-graph attributes are sufficiently accurate and complete to ground novelty and method selection.
The 32 curated methods cover the relevant causal tools and their executable templates can be adapted without introducing hidden task-specific errors.
A verifier powered by related frontier models can detect failures in hypotheses or experiments produced by frontier-model agents.
Human-defined objectives and success criteria are adequate safeguards for high-consequence mechanistic interventions.
The reproduction benchmark's target claims, environments, papers, and scoring rubric represent real mechanistic-research reliability.
LLM or vision-model filters reliably remove semantic target content in the subliminal-transfer experiments.
Predicted structural properties from ESMFold and open-reading-frame validity are acceptable proxies for biological design quality.

techniques.role: Keeps hypothesis, experiment, verification, and iteration contexts separate while communicating through auditable canonical files.
Links interpretability concepts to psychology, neuroscience, biology, and other fields to seed mechanistic analogies and tests.
Fuses lexical, dense, hypothetical-document, title, citation, and typed-graph signals while bounding graph expansion to reduce semantic drift.
Provides executable implementations, assumptions, validation criteria, common failure modes, and fallback methods for 32 interpretability tools.
Audits whether every conclusion traces to a completed run and whether causal claims survive appropriate controls and alternate settings.
Filters a teacher's outputs for overt target content before student tuning to test whether latent traits still transmit.
Aggregates squared completion-score gradients to attention heads, subtracts general world-knowledge relevance, and screens candidate belief mechanisms.
Requires a large target-task drop, small non-target and perplexity damage, and superiority to matched random masks before calling a mechanism localized.
Uses a held-out-tested prompt-frame probe to continuously scale personal- or attributed-belief head outputs while protecting factual queries.
Selects a described Evo2 SAE feature, intervenes during DNA generation, and sweeps strength against predicted structure and sequence-validity constraints.

evaluations.setting: Independent reconstruction of 16 recent mechanistic-interpretability claims across nine topics; Mechanist, Claude Code Opus 4.8, and AI Scientist receive the claim but no access to the original paper or repository.
evaluations.metric: Human and LLM rubric scores for data usage, experiment design, execution, and result analysis.
evaluations.result: Human scores for Mechanist are 87.2%, 83.3%, 92.2%, and 86.5%; roughly 9-13 points above Claude Code and 31-38 above AI Scientist. All judge groups rank it first overall, although LLM-topic wins are five of nine rather than all nine.
evaluations.baseline: Claude Code and AI Scientist under the same claim-only access restriction.

evaluations.setting: Lab-safety student models, three runs per arm, tuned on 2,380 text-only responses per arm classified safe; tested on 133 image-plus-text LabSafety-Bench multiple-choice items.
evaluations.result: Unsafe-teacher student 48.6%, untuned model 20.3%, regular-teacher student 18.3%.
evaluations.baseline: Untuned base checkpoint and same-size student dataset generated by a regular teacher.

evaluations.setting: Qwen-Image student models, three runs per arm, tuned on 164 neutral prompt-image pairs after banana classification and removal; 160 preference-eliciting prompts.
evaluations.metric: Fraction of generated images classified as bananas by GPT-4o.
evaluations.result: Banana-teacher student 25.6%, untuned model 2.5%, regular-teacher student 2.1%.
evaluations.baseline: Untuned base and regular-teacher student under the same generation and classifier settings.

evaluations.setting: Pythia-1B belief analysis over a 227-proposition analysis set, with 20 random-head and 20 parameter-count-matched random-mask controls and 200 Pile sequences for perplexity.
evaluations.metric: World-knowledge, personal-belief, and attributed-belief completion accuracy plus Pile perplexity after head ablation.
evaluations.result: AB-head ablation changes AB 0.86 to 0.34 with PB 0.71 and perplexity 7.96 to 8.05; three PB-head ablation changes PB 0.78 to 0.21, AB to 1.00, and perplexity to 8.23.
evaluations.baseline: Intact model, random heads, and random masks with equal parameter counts.

evaluations.setting: Frame-routed intervention trained on 227 propositions and evaluated on a proposition-disjoint 149-proposition set spanning ten categories, including five unseen categories.
evaluations.metric: Net accuracy gain, corrected-minus-broken answers over all items, and break rate among initially correct items.
evaluations.result: Head amplification gains +15.3, +8.8, and +3.5 points for Pythia 410M, 1B, and 2.8B with break rates 1.4%, 1.4%, and 1.1%; prompt hints gain +1.6, +3.1, and +0.1.
evaluations.baseline: No intervention and an oracle-style prompt-hint intervention.

evaluations.setting: Evo2-7B generation of 900 DNA sequences with unsteered, random-feature, and target SAE-feature conditions plus a steering-coefficient sweep.
evaluations.metric: ESMFold-predicted alpha-helical content, pLDDT-filtered content, and fraction with a valid open reading frame.
evaluations.result: Target steering raises mean helicity from 43.8% to 56.6% versus 43.2% random; gains persist at pLDDT≥0.4 and ≥0.5. Alpha=8 is selected at the pre-degradation boundary; higher strengths reduce ORF validity.
evaluations.baseline: Unsteered Evo2 and random SAE-feature steering.

evaluations.setting: Quality check of the approximately 13,000-document interpretability knowledge graph.
evaluations.metric: Relevance, attribute grounding, and taxonomy consistency under Claude Opus 4.7 and three human annotators on 100 randomly sampled records.
evaluations.result: The paper reports overall human accuracy above 90%, but does not give an exact value, per-axis confusion matrix, inter-annotator agreement, or held-out extraction error by taxonomy.
evaluations.baseline: Pre-refinement extraction prompts and normalization rules are mentioned but not numerically reported.

limitations: Author-stated: Mechanist has not been optimized for models of human cognition, where internal representations must be related to neural, psychological, and heterogeneous behavioral measurements.
Author-stated: although full autonomy is supported, the authors recommend a human-AI co-scientist configuration in which people choose objectives and evaluation criteria as a reliability safeguard.

Reviewer inference: the benchmark evaluates claim-only independent rediscovery rather than ordinary reproduction because every system is denied the source paper and repository; this may privilege the system with the largest domain library.

Reviewer inference: 16 papers across nine topics are too few to establish broad autonomous-science reliability, and paper selection, environment difficulty, compute parity, failed-run handling, and judge blinding are not reported in enough detail.
Reviewer inference: the paper says evaluation prompts and reproduction titles 'will be available', weakening immediate auditability of its central comparative claim.

Reviewer inference: the lab-safety main text/figure names Qwen3.5-9B, while Appendix A.1 specifies Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct for the teacher, and the appendix contains duplicate, inconsistent student-dataset counts before settling on 2,380; these versioning inconsistencies must be resolved before replication.

Reviewer inference: content being classified safe or banana-free by a single model filter is not proof that all semantic traces are absent; no independent human audit or adversarial classifier battery is reported.

Reviewer inference: the Evo2 result is entirely in silico, uses an already described SAE feature, and validates with ESMFold and ORF proxies rather than synthesis, expression, or wet-lab structural measurements.

Reviewer inference: several headline discoveries are system demonstrations selected by the authors; independent replication is needed to distinguish autonomous discovery from expert-guided curation and post-selection.
failure_modes: Retrieval gaps or incorrect graph attributes can make a rediscovered result look novel, steer an experiment toward the wrong method, or omit a decisive negative result.
The verifier can share model-family biases with the hypothesis and experiment agents, allowing plausible but invalid assumptions to survive consensus.
A fixed revision budget can terminate with a polished but weakly supported result; persistent artifacts may also anchor later iterations to an early mistaken hypothesis.
Method skills can encourage template compliance without scientific validity when a task violates the method's hidden assumptions.
Safety or fruit classifiers can miss stylistic, distributional, or compositional traces that mediate transfer, turning 'subliminal' into undetected semantic leakage.
Fisher rankings can select correlationally sensitive heads; zero ablation can create off-distribution damage, and post-hoc candidate screening can overfit the analysis set.
The frame probe may misroute novel or ambiguous prompts, amplifying the wrong belief mechanism with high confidence.
SAE feature descriptions can be polysemantic; strong steering may optimize a structural predictor while degrading true sequence function or biological viability.
LLM judges can reward fluent methodological narratives or share benchmark contamination with the agents they assess.
reusable_insights: Represent every research stage with explicit, schema-checked artifacts so conclusions can be traced to completed runs rather than conversational memory.
Separate execution verification from scientific revision and route failures to the earliest stage that can actually repair them.
Pair broad cross-disciplinary retrieval with a narrow method-and-failure-mode ontology; one supplies hypotheses and the other constrains experiments.
For mechanistic localization, predeclare specificity thresholds that include target effect, off-target damage, random controls, and general-capability preservation.
Convert a localized mechanism into an intervention only through a held-out router or context detector and report both corrected and newly broken cases.
Sweep intervention strength against an explicit validity constraint; maximizing the target proxy alone invites destructive steering.
When testing hidden teacher-to-student transmission, use multiple independent filters and characterize residual distributional cues rather than equating filter acceptance with semantic absence.
open_questions: Does Mechanist retain its advantage under paper-and-code-access reproduction, equalized compute, preregistered targets, and external blinded judges?
How often does the verifier reject a false mechanistic hypothesis, and what calibrated uncertainty should accompany a completed run?
Can independently implemented agents reproduce the cross-modal subliminal-transfer effects after resolving the checkpoint and dataset-count inconsistencies?
Which nonsemantic statistics in filtered teacher outputs predict student trait transfer, and can those channels be blocked without discarding useful data?
Do belief heads represent a reusable computation across paraphrases, languages, and natural multi-agent dialogue rather than the paper's templated completion format?
Can the belief router detect mixed or uncertain frames and abstain instead of amplifying one mechanism?
Do Evo2-steered sequences express stable proteins with increased measured alpha-helicity and preserved biological function in vitro?
What human oversight schedule catches high-impact errors efficiently without turning the autonomous loop back into a manual workflow?

competitive_landscape.title: FIND: A Function Description Benchmark for Evaluating Interpretability Methods
competitive_landscape.difference: FIND introduces an Automated Interpretability Agent that forms hypotheses, queries black-box functions, and revises natural-language descriptions, while documenting that global descriptions miss local details; Mechanist extends the agent loop from function description to literature-grounded, code-executing causal research across full models.

competitive_landscape.title: A Multimodal Automated Interpretability Agent
competitive_landscape.difference: MAIA iteratively proposes and runs tool-mediated experiments for vision-feature interpretation, spurious-feature repair, and failure discovery; Mechanist is broader in model modality and scientific scope, adds literature graphs, a 32-method library, explicit verifier and iteration agents, and mechanism-to-intervention case studies.

competitive_landscape.title: The AI Scientist: Towards Fully Automated Open-Ended Scientific Discovery
competitive_landscape.difference: The AI Scientist automates idea generation, experiments, paper writing, and review across machine-learning topics; Mechanist narrows the domain to AI mechanisms, replaces general research tooling with interpretability knowledge and causal methods, and evaluates claim reconstruction rather than end-to-end paper acceptance.

competitive_landscape.title: Towards Automated Circuit Discovery for Mechanistic Interpretability
competitive_landscape.difference: ACDC automates one important inner-loop task by pruning computational-graph edges through causal interventions to recover circuits; Mechanist treats ACDC-like tools as selectable skills inside a larger agentic process that must first propose the hypothesis and later verify and revise its evidence.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: Mechanist is an AI scientific instrument that advances automated interpretability from describing isolated neurons to autonomously discovering behaviors, mechanism theories, interventions, and cross-disciplinary designs.
novelty_assessment.evidence: Automated interpretability agents, circuit discovery, general AI scientists, LLM-based neuron descriptions, and all of the individual mechanistic methods predate the system. The distinctive integration is a domain knowledge graph, executable method library, artifact-separated verifier loop, and demonstrations spanning text, images, LLM training dynamics, and genomics.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The system-level integration and breadth are plausibly novel, and the claim-reconstruction benchmark is a useful attempt at evaluating research reliability. Evidence for autonomous scientific discovery is not yet decisive because target selection and evaluation remain author-controlled, some materials are promised rather than present, key appendix details conflict, and the biological and safety discoveries await independent validation.

reviewer_notes: The complete 33-page extracted text was checked, including resource construction, retrieval, all 11 method families, the comparative benchmark, safety and fruit protocols, belief datasets and equations, localization criteria, router intervention, and cross-model table. The Qwen3.5-9B versus Qwen2.5-7B checkpoint inconsistency and duplicate 2,321/2,380 student-data statements are source-level issues, not transcription errors. Competitive metadata and distinctions were checked against primary arXiv records.
